To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We propose a novel framework in which the sequence decomposition of the target sequence is learned during training.
1) We present Latent Sequence Deco-mpositions (LSD) which is a framework in which a sequence decomposition is learnt during the train-ing of a sequence-to-sequence model.

(1) Latent Sequence Decomposition models achieve state-of-the-art results on the WSJ dataset, and (2) LSD models can be combined with convolutional networks on the encoder, and (3) the LSD model can be trained end-to-end with a convolutional neural network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do we learn the latent sequence decomposition? How do we train a sequence-to-sequence model that uses this latent sequence decomposition?
the problem of how to decompose sequences in sequence-to-sequence models.
learning the latent sequence decomposition, which can be seen as a generalization of the sequence to sequence models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LSD model achieves a WER of around 10% with a 3x speedup over a character baseline.
our LSD model achieves a 3.3% WER improvement over a character baseline and 2.2% WER improvement when combined with convolutional layers.
LSD models achieve a 12.9-9.6% WER, which represents a 3.2% relative reduction in the WER compared to the character model, and a 2.2% relative improvement in WER compared to our best baseline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach for sequence-to-sequence modeling, where the decomposition is not fixed, but rather is learned during training.
the LSD framework is a general framework that can be applied to different domains and tasks.
we propose an approach that allows for a dynamic sequence decomposition, and show that the resulting model is able to achieve better performance than a character baseline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn an adaptive tokenization scheme for sequence-to-sequence models.
a sequence-to-sequence model can be trained to learn the optimal decomposition of the target sequence into constituent tokens.
the choice of tokens for a particular problem is not fixed, and should be learned from the training data.
